claim: Neonatal meningitis is associated with a mortality rate of 10-15%
source: Neonatal meningitis (NM) is a devastating disease with a mortality rate of 10–15% and severe neurological sequelae including hearing loss, reduced motor skills, and impaired development in 30–50% of cases (Doctor et al., 2001; Stevens et al., 2003; Harvey et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies (Doctor et al., 2001; Stevens et al., 2003; Harvey et al., 1999)

evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Harvey et al., 1999

claim: Escherichia coli is the second most common cause of neonatal meningitis in full-term infants after group B Streptococcus
source: Escherichia coli is the second most common cause of NM in full-term infants (herein NMEC), after group B Streptococcus (GBS) (Ouchenir et al., 2017; Gaschignard et al., 2011), and the most common cause of meningitis in preterm neonates (Gaschignard et al., 2011; Basmaci et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies (Ouchenir et al., 2017; Gaschignard et al., 2011)

claim: Escherichia coli is the most common cause of meningitis in preterm neonates

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies (Gaschignard et al., 2011; Basmaci et al., 2015)

claim: Group B Streptococcus and E. coli together cause approximately 60% of all neonatal meningitis cases
source: Together, these two pathogens cause ~60% of all cases, with on average one case of NMEC for every two cases of GBS (May et al., 2005; Holt et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies (May et al., 2005; Holt et al., 2001)

claim: On average, there is one case of NMEC for every two cases of GBS neonatal meningitis
source: Together, these two pathogens cause ~60% of all cases, with on average one case of NMEC for every two cases of GBS (May et al., 2005; Holt et al., 2001).

claim: Neonatal meningitis incidence caused by GBS has declined in several countries due to maternal intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis
source: In several countries, NM incidence caused by GBS has declined due to maternal intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis; however, NM incidence caused by E. coli remains the same (May et al., 2005; van der Flier, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published studies (May et al., 2005; van der Flier, 2021)

claim: Neonatal meningitis incidence caused by E. coli remains the same despite maternal intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis

claim: Approximately 80% of NMEC express the K1 capsule

claim: A collection of 58 NMEC isolates was established spanning 1974-2020 from seven different geographic regions
source: A collection of 52 NMEC isolates cultured from the blood or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of neonates with meningitis was established with the addition of six completely sequenced NMEC genomes available on the NCBI database. This yielded a final set of 58 NMEC isolates spanning 1974–2020. The isolates were obtained from seven different geographic locations; Finland (n = 17, 29.3%), Sweden (n = 14, 24.1%), Australia (n = 15, 25.9%), Cambodia (n = 7, 12.1%), USA (n = 3, 5.2%), France (n = 1, 1.7%), and the Netherlands (n = 1, 1.7%).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text describing the study collection
